<DIV><FONT size="1" style="font-size:1pt;color:white">For news releases, related materials and high-resolution photos and video, visit www.media.ford.com.  Growing Electric, Hybrid, Truck Sales Back Q3 Gains; Ford No. 1 Brand  &#8226; Ford Motor Company U.S. retail sales climb 4% in Q3, with overall sales up 1%, compared to a 2% decline for the total industry  &#8226; Ford is the No. 2 electric vehicle brand in the U.S. with sales up 12% in Q3; Ford commanded  highest transaction prices of all non-luxury electric vehicle brands &#8226; Ford is No. 1 in hybrid trucks with a 77% segment share; total hybrid sales up 38% &#8226; Ford, America&#8217;s best-selling brand in Q3, is also No. 1 in the following segments: trucks (F-Series), hybrid trucks (F-150 Hybrid), vans (Transit), three-row SUVs (Explorer) and sports cars (Mustang)  &#8226; Ford Pro Intelligence software platform active subscriptions up an estimated 30% year-over-year DEARBORN, Mich., Oct. 2, 2024 &#8211; Ford and Lincoln's strategy of offering customers a choice of  powertrains for their vehicles continues to pay off, with company retail sales up 4% in the third quarter.  This contrasts with overall U.S. retail industry sales, estimated to be flat for the quarter.  Total Ford sales outpaced the industry, rising 1% compared with a 2% decline for the overall market.  Customers continued to favor hybrid vehicles during the summer months. Sales increased 38% to 48,101  in the third quarter, while electric vehicle sales grew 12%. These results come before customers can take  advantage of the new Ford Power Promise which includes a complimentary home charger with  standard installation at no extra charge, and access to a 24/7 Ford advisor for electric vehicle support.  &#8220;Different lifestyles and use cases require unique types of power,&#8221; said Andrew Frick, president, Ford Blue  and Ford Customer Service Division. &#8220;We&#8217;ve listened to customers to offer them vehicles with powertrains  to meet their specific needs, and their response validates our product strategy.&#8221;  Truck Leadership Continues  The Ford F-Series exemplifies the Ford Freedom of Choice strategy, boasting an unmatched powertrain  lineup. With gas and diesel-powered Super Duty trucks and the light-duty F-150 &#8212; available in gas, hybrid  and electric &#8212; F-Series sales totaled 550,835 through September. The F-Series now outsells the Chevrolet  Silverado by 138,000 and the Ram by 282,000 trucks, expanding its lead as it aims to be America&#8217;s best- selling truck lineup for the 48th consecutive year in 2024.  Best-Selling Hybrids  F-150 hybrid sales rose 64% in the third quarter to 20,129, making it the best-selling hybrid truck. It topped another Ford model, the Maverick, which saw sales rise 22% to 16,561. The two trucks combined  account for 77% of the hybrid pickup segment.  Lincoln Nautilus Q3 Sales Best in 17 Years  Lincoln sales accelerated in the third quarter, up 26%, driven by the continued strength of the all-new  Nautilus and the launch of the new Aviator.  </FONT></DIV>

<DIV><FONT size="1" style="font-size:1pt;color:white">    For news releases, related materials and high-resolution photos and video, visit www.media.ford.com.      2 Nautilus sales totaled 8,799, its best third-quarter performance since 2007. For the quarter, Nautilus  hybrids represented 46% of all Nautilus sales (4,046), up 12% compared with the second quarter.  Aviator sales totaled 5,543, with the new SUVs spending an average of 16 days on dealer lots.  New Explorer Sales Up 25%  Sales of the new Ford Explorer launched in the third quarter. Explorer totaled 41,996, up 25%. Year-to- date, Explorer sales are up 6%, and it remains America&#8217;s best-selling three-row SUV.  Year-to-date, sales of the larger Ford Expedition rose 3%, while sales of the smaller Escape climbed 7%.  Ford will debut an all-new Expedition on Oct. 3.  Ford Electric Vehicles Continue to Rise  Ford brand electric vehicle sales are up 45% this year, second only to Tesla in the U.S. market. With  67,689 electric vehicles sold through September, Ford&#8217;s electric vehicles are having a record sales run.  Sales of the electric F-150 Lightning more than doubled, helping overall Ford electric vehicle sales post a  12% quarterly gain. America&#8217;s best-selling electric van, the Ford E-Transit, posted a 13% gain on sales of  2,955 vans.  In the third quarter, Ford brand electric vehicles had the highest transaction prices of all non-luxury  electric vehicle brands. Ford maintains a lease mix that is currently 35 percentage points below that of the  overall electric vehicle segment, helping to better support residual values.  Ford Pro Vehicles, Intelligence Software Sales Up  F-Series Super Duty sales increased 12% compared with a year ago and are up 9% through September.  Ford vans account for 52% of the full-size van segment so far in 2024 as the company looks to make it 46  consecutive years as a leader in that segment.  As America&#8217;s No. 1-selling van, Transit sales totaled 114,281 through September &#8212; up 17% over the same  nine-month period last year.  Ford was No. 1 in commercial vehicle sales based on the most recent registration data through July. Ford  U.S. Class 1-7 commercial truck and van share grew to 42.5%, up 2 percentage points compared with the  same period last year.  The Ford Pro Intelligence software platform now has approximately 620,000 active subscriptions, based  on end-of-quarter estimates, up about 30% year-over-year.  Remote Services Continue Rapid Growth  Ford and Lincoln dealers provided customers with more than 1 million remote service experiences in the  third quarter. These include Mobile Service &#8212; in which technicians drive to service a customer&#8217;s vehicle &#8212;  and Pickup &amp; Delivery &#8212; in which a dealer employee picks up, services and returns a customer&#8217;s vehicle.  Dealers have provided more than 2.8 million remote service experiences during the first nine months of  2024, up 118% compared with the same period a year ago.  </FONT></DIV>

The company&#8217;s Ford+ plan for growth and  value creation combines existing strengths, new capabilities and always-on relationships with customers to enrich  experiences for customers and deepen their loyalty.
